requirements.title: Intrinsic Fortran type parameters interoperate with the C types named in Table 18.2
requirements.definition: A Fortran intrinsic type with a particular kind type parameter, and character length one for character, is interoperable with a listed C type exactly on the corresponding Table 18.2 row; such a combination is also interoperable with compatible unqualified C types.

pending.table-row-type-kind-correspondence: Table-driven mixed Fortran/C plan enumerates every standardized Table 18.2 named constant: C_INT, C_SHORT, C_LONG, C_LONG_LONG, C_SIGNED_CHAR, C_SIZE_T, C_INT8_T, C_INT16_T, C_INT32_T, C_INT64_T, C_INT_LEAST8_T, C_INT_LEAST16_T, C_INT_LEAST32_T, C_INT_LEAST64_T, C_INT_FAST8_T, C_INT_FAST16_T, C_INT_FAST32_T, C_INT_FAST64_T, C_INTMAX_T, C_INTPTR_T, C_PTRDIFF_T, C_FLOAT, C_DOUBLE, C_LONG_DOUBLE, C_FLOAT_COMPLEX, C_DOUBLE_COMPLEX, C_LONG_DOUBLE_COMPLEX, C_BOOL, C_CHAR. For each constant, first test k > 0; only the positive branch declares the corresponding Fortran kind and C companion type. C writes exact load-bearing values such as 37 for integer rows, -4.5 or 1.5 for real rows, (2.0,-3.0) for complex rows, true for C_BOOL, and Z for C_CHAR; Fortran variables start from distinct sentinels and verify the exact changed values or exact component values. Negative branches record unsupported rows and never declare or write a literal of that kind.
pending.character-length-one-correspondence: Mixed plan uses a C char set to Q and a Fortran CHARACTER(KIND=C_CHAR,LEN=1) BIND(C) scalar initialized to X; after the C write, Fortran expects Q. Source-control companion changes only LEN=1 to LEN=2 and records that no required diagnostic is owned here.
pending.unqualified-compatible-c-type-correspond: Mixed plan declares the C companion objects without const/volatile qualification for the same positive rows and verifies the same Fortran kind receives exact values; a future qualified-C source-use variant may document compatibility without asserting extra Fortran syntax.

requirements.title: ISO_C_BINDING named-constant signs determine intrinsic interoperable combinations
requirements.definition: The second Table 18.2 column names ISO_C_BINDING constants; a negative value means no Fortran type and type-parameter combination interoperates with that C type, while positive values identify usable Fortran kind type parameter values.

requirements.title: Support for Table 18.2 C rows and exact kind values is processor latitude
requirements.definition: A processor can expose a negative ISO_C_BINDING named constant for a Table 18.2 C row, meaning that no interoperable Fortran combination exists for that C type; positive kind values are usable through the named constants without fixing their exact integer values.

pending.c-row-support-processor-latitude: No portable oracle may require support for C_LONG_DOUBLE, C_INT128_T-like extensions, or any row whose ISO_C_BINDING constant is negative; future fixtures guard optional rows and assert only positive-row behavior.
pending.kind-value-exact-number-processor-latitu: No portable oracle may require C_INT, C_DOUBLE, or any other named constant to have a particular positive integer value; future fixtures compare equality of values obtained from ISO_C_BINDING and the C companion, not literal kind numbers.

requirements.title: Intrinsic type and type-parameter combinations inherit interoperability from C-type interoperability
requirements.definition: A combination of intrinsic type and type parameters is interoperable exactly by virtue of being interoperable with a C type; the C types named in Table 18.2 are the referenced ISO C types.

Negative rows are skipped without declaring that kind.
pending.c-type-definitions-referenced: Source-use inventory plan records the exact ISO C type spelling used by the companion for each Table 18.2 positive row; no Fortran execution can prove the external ISO C definitions themselves.
